findings.title: Keeping `pendingInit` after an offline edit lets a later adoption silently drop that edit
findings.body:
An offline edit of a `pendingInit` workspace now keeps `pendingInit` and also sets `pendingIdentity` (lines 634, 638). Suppose the folder comes back holding an identity with another, unregistered id, for example one written by another Mac. `availability` then takes the adoption branch (lines 718-726): `Object.assign(entry, entryFromIdentity(...))` replaces the registry's newer name and color with the folder's values. It clears `pendingInit` but leaves `pendingIdentity` set. The next probe matches ids and "catches up" the file with values that are already the folder's (lines 670-682), so the user's rename is gone and nothing tells them.

Before this commit the edit cleared `pendingInit`, so this folder was reported as `different` and the rename was kept. The trigger is rare and needs the case you already deferred (another id in the folder). Two possible fixes: when `pendingIdentity` is set, keep the registry's name and color in the adoption branch, or refuse the adoption. Either way, also clear `pendingIdentity` there.

findings.title: No renderer test covers the suppressed toast for an unchanged relocate
findings.body: The main side asserts `unchanged: true` (`relocate.test.ts:158`). No renderer test checks that `onRelocated` skips the `folderChanged` toast when `unchanged` is set, or that it still shows the toast otherwise. A search of the renderer tests finds no assertion on `folderChanged` at all. That early return is the user-visible fix from the earlier thread, so a regression there would go unnoticed. A small `WorkspacesProvider` test (Change folder… resolving `{ ok: true, unchanged: true }` shows no toast; `{ ok: true }` shows one) would pin it.

contracts.action: Change folder… on the folder the workspace already points at returns `unchanged: true`, and the renderer shows no toast
contracts.equivalent_path: The non-active branch `registry.relocate` and the active branch `relocateActive`, which both return `{ ok: true, entry }` with no flag
contracts.before_after: `checkRelocate` still runs first, so refusals are unchanged. The early return skips the transaction. `relocateFolder` still runs the `availability` probe, `refreshTitles` and `broadcastState` afterwards, so an identity file deleted by hand is rewritten and the state is re-sent.
contracts.visible_effect: `relocateFolder` passes the flag through to the IPC result. Both callers (the dialog at workspace-dialog.tsx:145 and `changeFolder` at workspaces-context.tsx:185) call `onRelocated`, which returns before `showToast` when `unchanged` is set. The row and dialog update through `broadcastState`.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected IPC call still shows `relocateUncertain` (workspaces-context.tsx:180-182). The early return writes nothing, so it cannot fail halfway.

contracts.action: An offline edit keeps `pendingInit` when the identity was not written to the folder
contracts.equivalent_path: `availability` clears `pendingInit` only once an identity is in the folder (lines 709, 725, 745)
contracts.before_after: `checkRelocate` keeps accepting a folder with Kaipu items and no identity (line 855). The probe after the move writes the identity under the registered id, with the edited name (lines 733-748). In the adoption branch (718-726), however, the folder's values overwrite the offline edit and `pendingIdentity` stays set.
contracts.visible_effect: The moved folder is accepted. If the folder holds another id, the rename is silently replaced by the folder's name.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed identity write in `availability` leaves the entry pending, and the next probe retries.

thread_replies.reply: Fixed. The rollback at registry.ts:643-647 restores the old file, or removes the new one when the folder had none.
Fixed. Name and color are now checked separately.
Fixed. `edit` re-runs the name check inside the locked `update` (registry.ts:626) and undoes the identity write on `NameTakenError`.

Fixed for the no-identity case: `checkRelocate` accepts it for `pendingInit` (registry.ts:855), and this round keeps `pendingInit` through an offline edit (line 634). The other-id case is deferred as you said. One side effect of keeping `pendingInit` is raised as a separate finding: the adoption branch can now drop an offline rename.
Acknowledged as a follow-up. The current code still drops pending captures in the relocate transaction, which is out of scope here.
Fixed. The same path now returns early, before `relocateActive` (relocate.ts:43-45).
Fixed. `unchanged: true` goes from relocate.ts:44 through index.ts:349 to workspaces-context.tsx:168, which skips the toast. A renderer test for it is suggested separately.

structuredOutput.summary: The round fixes both points it set out to fix. Picking the current folder in Change folder… now returns `unchanged: true` from main to the renderer, and no misleading toast appears. An offline edit of a `pendingInit` workspace keeps the flag, so the moved folder is still accepted, and the new registry test pins that. Two findings, both at "consider": keeping `pendingInit` lets the adoption branch in `availability` silently replace an offline rename and leave `pendingIdentity` set, and no renderer test covers the suppressed toast. Of the earlier threads, six are addressed; the dropped-capture one stays open as an acknowledged follow-up.
